title: NICHD says a newborn can tell the mother's voice from other sounds
summary: An NICHD spotlight says that at birth, babies can tell their mother's voice from other sounds around them.
body: The NICHD early-learning spotlight of 10 August 2017 says that at birth, babies can tell the difference between their mother's voice and other sounds from the world around them. The sentence is the spotlight's summary. The paragraph does not name the study beside that sentence. It is not a claim about every sound a newborn can sort, and it is not a hearing-screening result. The page is a United States institute spotlight.

sources.title: Focus on Early Learning
sources.author: Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development
sources.note: US federal page, public domain. Opened 2026-11-26. Page dated Thursday, 10 August 2017. Supports the sentence that at birth babies can tell the mother's voice from other sounds.
